answer: An AI-agent economy can resist Sybil attacks using network multilateration mapped to a latency atlas. Distributed beacons issue timed challenges, using speed-of-light bounds to enforce unique physical coordinates per agent. Whether deploying a falcon drone or a glacier sensor, an attacker incurs the scarce cost of provisioning distinct physical network interfaces per identity. However, this mechanism disadvantages legitimate co-located agents and cannot prevent low-latency relay proxies.
